args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in production in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. The service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

**Rollback**
- **Why v2.3.0:** It's the most recent release that was healthy in production. The bad release, v2.3.1, failed health checks everywhere with an 18% error rate. Its test build (v2.3.1-rc) had also failed health checks in staging before it went out.
- **Result:** All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now run v2.3.0. After the rollback, the service passes health checks and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Approval:** None was needed, because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before.

**Incident INC-0001 (SEV2, open, on-call paged)**
- It records the failure, the rollback to v2.3.0 and the recovery numbers. It also says the root cause in v2.3.1 needs to be found before anyone redeploys it.
- My first attempt to open it timed out. The incident list was still empty afterwards, so I tried again using the same duplicate-prevention key as the first attempt. Only one incident exists, so the on-call engineer was paged once.
